_about: Hand-written node content for the dungeons of data/dungeons/dungeons.json (the CSV import). Everything here is placeholder-grade text and numbers (balance is out of scope). Per dungeon: defaults (deck archetypes, icons, AIs cycled over its battles), boss (deck/hp/icon), foes (node number -> foe name, or an object {name, deck, size, hp, ai, icon, extra}), events / challenges / loot (node number -> content), blurbs, story_keys (node number -> story key `dungeon.<key>.before/.after`, in the zone story file or in `text` below), scenes (node number -> {before, after} cutscene ids). Event/challenge effects are tokens: heal:N damage:N gold:N pay:N lose:N card:ID boon:Name|max_hp=2,atk=1,def=1,start_hp=1 (curse:Name|max_hp=-1 is the same with negative numbers) rescue sever. An event may be {ref: id} naming one the dungeon class still builds in code.

5.title: Locker Room of Legends
5.body: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, and something inside is humming a marching tune to itself.
choices: The towel is still warm and smells of eucalyptus and somebody else's victory. You feel sturdier with it round your neck, and very slightly watched.
Inside are protein bars, a roll of gold and a note that says 'Spotter knows.' Somewhere down the hall a whistle blows, and you leave with the gold and a guilty conscience.
Do a set with the ghost of a champion
The ghost miscounts your reps on purpose, always upward, to be encouraging. You walk away standing taller, if not stronger, and he presses a Gym Bro's number into your hand.

12.title: The Sauna of Truth
12.text: The steam asks one honest question: how hard do you lead?

7.title: The Corrupted Pantry
7.body: Shelves of glowing, sickly-green food hum softly. A ladle is still stirring a pot that nobody is minding, and the pot has started to hum back.
choices: It is delicious and almost certainly cursed. You feel strong and slightly sticky, and your units will not stop smelling of gravy.
A few shelves are still clean, stacked with jars labelled DO NOT OPEN, WE MEAN IT. You respect their wishes and sell them unopened.
It has been stirring for ten years and nobody ever asked it to stop. It sighs, hands you a Sourdough Sentry out of gratitude, and finally rests.

10.title: R&D Archives
10.body: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate without a single gravy stain, and a real chef's notes are mostly gravy stain.
choices: Laid beside the old recipe cards, it is plain: whoever signed these memos has never held a ladle. The person giving orders in this kitchen is not the cook who used to.
Blueprints like these are evidence, and evidence always has a buyer. The one you find asks no questions, which is the best kind.
Pocket the recipe marked DO NOT SERVE
It is one line long and ends with 'send it back.' You can see why it was classified.

4.title: Taste Test Lab
4.text: Beakers, spoons and a very small flag: does your deck have the body for the panel?

blurbs.11: The cannon-blender is fed protein and plates in equal measure. Every Ingredient and every Iron goes into the same shaker, and something six feet tall comes out.

2.title: Take-a-Number Kiosk
2.body: A small grey machine offers you ticket 4,000,213 while the display above says NOW SERVING 3. A polite ghost behind you coughs, then apologises for coughing.
choices: You wait, and then you wait some more, until a vending machine takes pity on you and dispenses one sad cookie.
The machine jams, apologises and coughs up coins and a written warning. You are now marked 'Difficult.'
Nobody dares object, at least not yet, and somewhere down the queue they have started whispering about Number 4,000,213.

8.title: Form 27-B Office
8.body: Form 27-B requires Form 27-C, which requires a stamp from the office you are standing in. A clerk slides a pen across the counter without looking up.
choices: Everything is in order. A boon is granted and a small tax is levied, in that order, by two different departments.
It works, mostly. Something in the ceiling disapproves loudly, with a stapler.
Ask the clerk what Form 27-C is
The clerk looks up for the first time in decades. Nobody has ever asked. She slides you a Pink Slip 'for personal use' and, you swear, winks.

12.title: The Shredding Room
12.body: Rows of paper shredders chew through the day's denied appeals. A sign reads: SHRED ONE THING, RECEIVE ONE THING. Another, in smaller letters, reads: THINGS INCLUDE YOU.
choices: The shredder hums happily and pays out in coins. It says 'denied' in a voice like a kettle.
Nothing is left of Number 4,000,213. You feel lighter and slightly nonexistent as the machine files you under 'Resolved.'
Reach in for what it ate
You pull out half of a lost appeal, which is technically a weapon, and the machine takes a bite of you in exchange.

5.title: Waiting Room of Eternity
5.text: Row after row of chairs stretches into the distance. Can your deck outwait the line?

blurbs.13: The elevator is hand-cranked by a Beefcake on loan from the wheels. Every floor needs a permit and a rep. Iron turns the crank; Red Tape keeps the doors shut.

7.title: Weeping Compost Pool
7.body: The pool is the colour of a bruise, and it's sobbing very quietly around a boot that bobs in the middle of it.
choices: It tastes of rain and old boots. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.
Somebody will pay good gold for a bottle of this. Down here, that somebody is usually a hedgehog.
You tell it that it's doing very well. It sobs harder, then gives you a very old Mulch Mole it was keeping safe, along with a little of its warmth.

12.title: The Heart Roots
12.body: Thick, pulsing roots run from every wall into the chamber beyond: the Rotheart's lifelines. You could cut them, and it would hurt her far more than you.
choices: The roots shriek and let go. Whatever waits ahead will be weaker for it.
The roots keep pulsing, and the Rotheart keeps its strength.

4.title: Strangled Greenhouse
4.text: The vines are choosing who gets through, and they're reading your deck very closely before they decide.

blurbs.10: The mutant bees have learned farming. What the rot throws away they turn into honey, and what they make they feed back to the rot.
blurbs.11: Something lifts in the Rot Tunnel. Every scrap of Garbage it finds becomes a rep, and every rep becomes Iron.

14.name: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News

3.title: Grand Foyer
3.body: A portrait of a smiling ruler fills the wall. The floor is so polished you can see yourself, and he is standing behind you in every reflection.
choices: The smile never changes, and neither, you realise, does anything else in this place. It is strangely restful, and that frightens you more than the guards do.
It is heavier than it looks and worth more than it should be, and now it is covered in your fingerprints, in a building that remembers fingerprints.
There is always one more reflection than there should be. You wave, he waves a moment too late, and for a moment you are a little less afraid of him.

12.title: The Doppelganger's Lab Notes
12.body: A lab table of food notes: a shapeshifter's recipe for becoming a Grand Chef, with an entire page on how to smile like her. The margins are full of practice smiles.
choices: It explains everything, including why the sauce tastes of nothing. There is no Grand Chef in here, only a very good understudy.
Somebody downstairs will pay for them and nobody upstairs will miss them, which is as much of a plan as you need.
Practise the smile in the mirror
The smile comes out perfect, which is horrifying, and your face stays like that for a while. The guards leave you alone.

22.title: Garden of Uniform Flowers
22.body: A thousand identical flowers stand in identical rows. You count them twice. One of them is, very slightly, a different shade of yellow.
choices: It tastes of dandelion. It feels like the first honest thing in the castle.
Pick a handful of the rest
They wilt in your hand and leave behind a few coins, which is more than they should have been able to do.
You press a bent stem into the soil. The gardener will find it tomorrow and have to rethink everything. You walk on, lighter.

S-IRON._note: Gainlands v2, Part F: the Iron Cave, tuned for the start of the game (small decks, low HP).

blurbs.2: The conveyor never stops, like the Eternal Queue it was modelled on. Each plate comes with a numbered ticket, stamped.
The Courtier collects the crusts the kingdom leaves behind and serves them back, warmed, as a royal tasting menu.
A Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs and Refusemancer drains all meet here, and the junction crew turns every scrap of Garbage into muscle.

3.name: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense

blurbs.1: Grey citizens queue for grey paste while a supervisor times every scoop of the ladle.
blurbs.2: The vats are the size of houses, and something in the third one is humming the national anthem.
blurbs.3: Behind the ration hatch is a real kitchen, with a locked pantry and a badger in medals standing guard over it.

4.title: The Observation Deck
4.body: A glass gallery looks down on the cells: a kettle, a cracked mug, and a corkboard of notes about one subject. The newest notes are only a count of days.
choices: Read the notes on the Subject
Drain cycles, power readings, a column labelled 'cooperative?' that someone has filled in with 'asks for his mother.' You put the notes down very carefully.
It is the first thing here that tastes like anything. You feel steadier.
Keycards, a petty cash tin, and a half-written resignation letter.

7.title: The Draining Chamber
7.body: A round chamber, glass on every side, a chair at the center with straps worn pale. Cables run from the chair to four great tanks, each glowing a different colour. This is where it was done.
choices: Put your hand on the glass
The four colors lean toward your palm like plants toward a window. They were yours. They remember.
Every cycle logged, every reading neat. You learn exactly how the machine works, which is how to break it.
They come away easily. They were only ever as strong as the people who buckled them.

12.title: The Mentor's Study
12.body: A warm, cluttered study with the only rug in the Lab. On the desk lies an open journal in a neat, slanted hand.
choices: Take the journal for Wren's true record
It goes into your pack, light as a confession.
Let him find it open. Let him wonder who read it.

6.title: Decontamination
6.text: Four nozzles hiss in four colors. A sensor asks whether your deck can carry more than one Path at a time.

S-GALLERY._note: Overnight Nov 4-5, Part 5: the Echoes play their originals' decks with more HP and a twisted rule each (data/encounters/modifiers.json); the boss is your own deck (ShatteredGallery.perfect_copy_setup).

3.title: The Weight of Glass
3.body: A barbell of solid mirror rests on a rack, and in every plate you see Clench at the height of his reign, lifting it easily. The rack has a little brass sign: FOR THE WORTHY.
choices: It's heavier than anything you've lifted, because it's made of everything he wanted to be. Your arms shake, then hold. Something in the glass looks away first.
You walk past. For the rest of the gallery, every reflection you pass is lifting it for you, slightly better.
The bar shatters into coins that are still warm. One of your cards goes with it, caught in the glass.

6.title: The Valid Reflection
6.body: A mirror in a gilt frame holds a form already filled in with your name, your Path and a box marked 'Approved'. A pen waits on a chain. The ink is still wet.
choices: The mirror stamps you APPROVED. You feel sturdier and a little less like yourself.
The frame lets out a long, disappointed sigh, and the glass at your back cuts you on the way past.
You sign 'Agnes Overdue'. The mirror has no answer to that and quietly pays you to leave.

8.title: The Quiet Frame
8.body: A frame with no glass in it, just a soft chair behind it and the sound of rain on a window that isn't there. It's the only quiet room in the gallery. A small plaque says RESTING IS A PRIVILEGE.
choices: You sit, and for a few minutes nothing reflects you at all. You stand up with steadier hands.
Rest, and leave a card as the fee
The chair keeps one of your cards in its cushion and lets you sleep.
You don't trust a quiet room in this place, and you're probably right.

12.title: Your Reflection
12.body: The last mirror before the end shows you as Primm would have made you: hair regulation length, posture perfect, smile approved. It's waiting to see what you'll do.
choices: It looks back, and for a second you can't tell which of you blinked. You take some of its certainty with you, and it takes some of your strength.
You walk on without looking. The glass behind you cracks a little louder than it should.
It breaks easily. Too easily. The pieces cut, and a shard of it goes on ahead of you to warn the room.

blurbs.1: The mirror at the castle door, cracked from the inside. Beyond it the air is cold and smells of polish.
blurbs.2: An Echo of Vivienne Quota, timing you to the second. Enemy units here enter with +1 attack.
blurbs.4: An Echo of Chancellor Clench, at the height of his reign. He starts with Iron already in hand.
blurbs.5: An Echo of Percival Plume, with perfectly good news. From here on the first card you play each turn costs 1 more.
blurbs.7: An Echo of Mortimer Grimsby. The authorization, he says, is reflected.
blurbs.9: An Echo of the Doppelganger, wearing a face it learned by heart. From here on the first unit you play each turn is copied for the enemy.
blurbs.10: An Echo of Hortensia Clipwell, in a garden trimmed so neatly it hurts.
blurbs.11: An Echo of the Rotheart, green glass that never stops growing.
blurbs.13: The Perfect Copy: your own deck, your own face, more HP and one extra card each turn.

quest.meet_the_merchants.active: Sable, Tilly and Pip, dearie, all three on the square. And buy a card from Sable while you're there. I'll not have you facing the roads with nothing but what a cave gave you.
quest.meet_the_merchants.ready: Back already? Let me guess: Sable charmed you, Tilly turned a colour, and Pip measured you before you'd finished saying hello. That's {town}, dearie.
Here, have a trophy. Everybody gets one, so don't let it go to your head. I made it myself, and the handle comes off if you wave it about.
quest.first_deck_edit.offer: Now, about that deck of yours. You didn't choose a single card in it, dearie, and a deck you never chose is a deck you'll lose with.
New cards first, so open a pack: the Menu at the top right, then Packs. Or press P, if you're the sort who presses things.
Then take it to the Deck Station, down Champions' Road south of the square. Swap in whatever you like, save it to a slot, and come and tell me how it went.
quest.first_deck_edit.offer_pack: No packs at all? Here, dearie, have a General Pack. It's been sat on a little. Cards are cards, and these ones won't hold it against you.
quest.first_deck_edit.active_pack: Open the pack first, dearie: the Menu, then Packs. It won't open itself. I've asked it nicely.
quest.first_deck_edit.active: The Deck Station is down Champions' Road, south of the square, dearie. Save it to a slot when you're done, or it doesn't count. I do check.
quest.first_deck_edit.ready: Sorted and saved, and every card in it your own choice. Good. Now when it loses, you've nobody to blame but yourself, which is how it ought to be.
quest.storeroom_ghosts.offer: Now, a favour. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been moaning for a week. I don't mean Tilly, dearie. I mean the room.
Ghosts, I expect, and petty ones, which are the worst kind. Nobody's been able to get in for so much as a candle. Go and sort them out, gently if they'll let you.
quest.storeroom_ghosts.active: The store room door is beside Tilly's shop, on the north side of the square. Ignore the rattling, dearie; that's just them being dramatic.
quest.storeroom_ghosts.ready: A refund? Ninety years of moaning, all over one broken lantern. I've had customers like that. I still have a few.
Well done, dearie. You've settled the ghosts, so now go and settle yourself somewhere dry before you catch a chill.
quest.some_assembly_required.offer: Right, then. It's time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth hands out gear from his smithy, on the west side of the square.
He is... thorough. Report to him, do what he asks, and do not touch his drawer.
quest.some_assembly_required.active: Bertram's smithy is on the west side of the square. Win him one fight, any fight at all, and he'll stamp something for you. He lives to stamp things.
quest.path_direction: Sit down a moment, dearie, before you go running off. It's time I pointed you somewhere properly. Start with {zone}. It's {path} country, and so, by the look of you, are you.
{vendor} sells more {path} cards out there than anyone in this town does, so take gold and a good big bag. And take my advice, for once.
Inside {zone}, your Path stands a little taller. {buff}: {buff_text}
The Paths quarrel, dearie: Beefcake against Necrocrat, Gourmand against Refusemancer. They always have. Once, they needed each other too much for it to matter.
So in {zone}, it's the {rival} side that gets the short end. {debuff}: {debuff_text} In {rival_zone}, it's the other way round, and you're the one who suffers.
{gatekeeper} holds {road} at {obstacle}, and nobody gets into {zone} without beating that fight first. Then come back alive. I'll have a pie waiting, and I don't bake for people who don't come back.
quest.side_s_town.offer: There is a door under the old well that has been locked since before I was born.
I always thought the key was lost, but it wasn't, dearie. Somebody hid it in a chest right here in town. Find it, and we'll see what the door is for.
quest.side_s_town.active: The key's in a hidden chest somewhere in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie; this town has never quite managed a straight one.
quest.side_s_town.ready: You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings in a ring. Hm. Never mind that. I'm too old for stairs, dearie, and you're not.
quest.side_s_town.done: The door's the iron hatch beside the well. Go on down. Whatever's under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me, so mind the stairs.
quest.side_s_beef.offer: Only the worthy reach the top, they say. The worthy also bring water, if they've any sense.

There's a mountain behind the station... and a barbell on top older than the regime. Older than me, nearly. Bring me a protein shake from the stand and I'll show you the way. Can't climb on an empty cup.
quest.side_s_beef.active: Water, friend. A protein shake from the stand will do. Don't spill it. I spilled one, the Festival year... where was I.
quest.side_s_beef.ready: That's the best water I've ever seen. Thank you. Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two... rule two was water.
quest.side_s_beef.done: Mount Swolympus is open at last. Take the trail behind the station, and mind the thin air up top... never gets enough credit, thin air.
quest.side_s_gour.offer: Over here, quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu at all? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.
There's a golden reservation card hidden in one of the Buffet's stashes: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Find it and I'll tell you where to sit.
quest.side_s_gour.active: The card's in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. It's golden, so you'll know it when you see it. Chef always said gold means sit down.
quest.side_s_gour.ready: That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited, I think - it feels a lot like being terrified.
quest.side_s_gour.done: The sliding door to Omakase is open. Leave your fate to the chef. (quietly) Yes, Chef.
quest.side_s_necro.offer: Number 4,000,212? That's me, and they're on 3. I don't suppose you could help?
The queue for the Waiting Room of Eternity is stuck. If you process two of the roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors, I can get you in. I'll wait. I'm very good at it.
quest.side_s_necro.active: Two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors, if you can. The queue won't move itself; I've given it a very fair chance.
quest.side_s_necro.ready: Two fewer, and the queue moved! Only slightly, but I felt it in my ticket.
quest.side_s_necro.done: The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number. Please leave mine; we've been through so much together.
quest.side_s_ref.offer: SOMEBODY has been eating ALL the compost. There are little paw prints everywhere, and next to the bin I found... a tiny crown.
Chase off two of the scavengers in the Dump and their trail should lead you to the big dumpster. Gently, please - they're only hungry. And GUILTY.
quest.side_s_ref.active: Two scavengers out in the Dump, please. Follow the fresh paw prints; it's a trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.
quest.side_s_ref.ready: The paw prints lead to the big dumpster. I knew it. I KNEW it.
quest.side_s_ref.done: Under the tipped-over dumpster there's a gate made from an old bicycle wheel, and that's the way to the Trash Panda Throne. Do bring a peg for your nose.
npc.kestrel.intro: Psst. Down. The enforcers walk this road on the hour, and they hate surprises. I'm a surprise.
Name's Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Heading into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow my chalk, not the guards; they're worse at drawing.
npc.kestrel.return: Road's clear for ten minutes. Chalk's fresh. Move while the guards are busy being punctual somewhere else.
quest.side_s_cap.offer: There's an older way into the city that nobody remembers. That's the whole point of it.
Get yourself inside and find Wren in the Crease. She'll tell you what the old tunnels are for. Then I'll show you the hatch. Deal?
quest.side_s_cap.active: Get inside, then find the manhole near the gate and knock three times. Not two; two is rude. Wren's down in the Crease. Ask her about the tunnels.
quest.side_s_cap.ready: So you found the Crease. Told you I'd be around; I just never said where. Here, you've earned this.
fx.old_tunnels_way_in: The grate beneath the plaza lifts with a groan. Light from the perfect city pours in, and behind you the old tunnels run on: four Paths' services, still connected.
You climb up inside the walls. Nobody is watching this way in, because nobody remembers it is here.
quest.side_s_cap.done: The hatch in the north-east of the Outskirts, under the wall, goes down to the Old Service Tunnels. Mind the patrols. And mind my chalk.
dungeon.dg_s_iron_boss.before: On a throne that is really a leg press, a Beefcake with thighs like mill wheels pushes a sled of plates up and down, up and down. He has not stood up in years.
'Nobody. Skips. Leg day.' He presses another rep. 'Not in my cave. Prove it. I won't get up.'
dungeon.dg_s_iron_boss.after: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says, looking down. 'So those are my feet. Hello, feet.'
He hands you a sweaty ribbon. 'Leg day survivor. Wear it. Stretch. That order.'
dungeon.dg_s_beef_boss.before: A stone colossus sits at the summit with its palms turned up, waiting for a barbell. It has been spotting for a thousand years, and it is very, very ready.
'Lift,' it rumbles. 'I will catch it. I have always caught it.'
dungeon.dg_s_beef_boss.after: The Ancient Spotter lowers its hands and, for the first time in a thousand years, sets something down. The barbell on the altar is yours.
'One more rep,' it says. Then, quieter: '...That was the one. Thank you for coming up.'
dungeon.dg_s_gour_boss.before: The Itamae Supreme lifts a long knife and does not look up. 'Omakase.'
Behind him, a bull made of toro lowers its horns, politely.
dungeon.dg_s_gour_boss.after: The Itamae bows, wipes his knife on a cloth and slides a small plate across the counter. 'Omakase,' he says. This time it sounds like thank you.
dungeon.dg_s_necro_boss.before: A single desk under a single green lamp, buried in forms. Betty Bones looks up through cat-eye glasses, very slowly, and sighs the sigh of the long deceased.
'Forms A through F,' she says. 'Then we'll talk. We won't, but still.'
dungeon.dg_s_necro_boss.after: Betty stamps one last form with a bony flourish. 'Fine. Number 4,000,212 is approved. Don't make it a thing.'
Far down the line, a ghost with a crumpled ticket begins, very quietly, to cheer.
dungeon.dg_s_ref_boss.before: The Throne of Lids creaks. On it sits a very large raccoon in a very small crown, sweating profusely.
'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We... sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
dungeon.dg_s_ref_boss.after: His Majesty abdicates with great dignity and a crust of pizza. The crown rolls under the throne.
'Compost is for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. We fail to see the problem. Do not point at the crumbs.'
dungeon.dg_s_cap_boss.before: A grate lets in light from a perfect city. Beneath it stands Captain Spotless, polishing his shield with a sleeve he has already polished.
'HALT. These tunnels do not exist, so you are standing in nothing, and I cannot allow you to have found it.'
dungeon.dg_s_cap_boss.after: The Captain sits down on a barrel and, for a moment, looks very tired. 'I remember when these tunnels were full of people,' he says.
'All four Paths, shoulder to shoulder, and nobody measuring anybody. Go on. The grate is not locked.'
dungeon.dg_s_town_boss.before: A four-coloured core hums at the heart of the vault, four marks set in a ring. Beside it a clockwork guardian unfolds, with a sound like a very old clock remembering the hour.
'Tick. Identify,' it says. 'The Old Kingdom's banner is not for just anyone.'
dungeon.dg_s_town_boss.after: The Automaton clicks, whirs and lowers one knee. In its outstretched hand, folded neatly, is the Old Kingdom's banner.
'Tick. ...Recognised. Four Paths. One kingdom. Carry it well.'
quest.cap_paste_works.offer: The dispenser's spoiled, and lovely it is too. But the paste has to come from somewhere, doesn't it?
The shuttered stall at the quarter's south-west corner hums at night, and stalls don't hum. Open its ration hatch and have a look down. Gently.
quest.cap_paste_works.active: It's the south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch, go down, and shut off whatever you find. I'd bet it's very, very grey.
quest.cap_paste_works.ready: You shut the vats down? All of them? Then tonight the whole quarter eats something that tastes of something.
Some taste. 'Some' is the best amount.
quest.cap_paste_works.done: I've kept one real onion in my apron for ten years, and tonight I'm chopping it. You may want to stand back. I'll be weeping, and not only from the onion.
event.lab_cell4.title: Cell 4
event.lab_cell4.body: Your old cell: ten years of tally marks, a child's drawing in four colors, and {rescuer} under it with her hands bound.
event.lab_cell4.result.0: The lock gives. She stands, rubs her wrists and looks at the drawing on the wall for a long moment before she looks at you.
dungeon.lab_cell4.title: Cell 4
cave_mouth.maren_path: One more thing before you go dripping on somebody else's floor. That deck of yours is {path} through and through, so start where it'll be easiest for you: {zone}.
Take {road} out of town. {gatekeeper} is standing at {obstacle}, and you'll have to win that duel before anyone lets you through. It's on your map, marked in your Path's colour.
The errands can wait as long as you like. The shops aren't going anywhere, and neither am I.
